question.problem: Find the directional derivative of the function $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+y\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ at the point $(1,1)$ in the direction of the vector $v=2i+j.$
question.worked_solution:
The directional derivative ${f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)$ of a function $f(x,y)$ at the point $(a,b)$ in the direction of the vector $v$ is given by

$$
{f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)=∇f(a,b)\cdot u
$$

where $u$ is a unit vector in the direction of $v.$

First, we find the unit vector $u$ in the direction of $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\sqrt{5} \\ u & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(2i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the gradient $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\text{ }j \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡y+\frac{y}{x})\,i+(\frac{x}{y}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\,j \\ ∇\,f(1,1) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡1+\frac{1}{1})\,i+(\frac{1}{1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\,j \\  & =i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the directional derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =∇\,f(1,1)\cdot u \\  & =(i+j)\cdot (\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}j) \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 2+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
